question.worked_solution:
The given function can be rewritten as follows:

$$
f(x)=\frac{10-3x-{x}^{2}}{17x+7}
$$

To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is $x.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{10-3x-{x}^{2}}{17x+7} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{10}{x}-\frac{3x}{x}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{x})}{(\frac{17x}{x}+\frac{7}{x})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{10}{x}-3-x)}{(17+\frac{7}{x})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{10}{x}$ and $\frac{7}{x}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{10}{x}-3-x)}{(17+\frac{7}{x})} \\  & ≈\frac{0-3-x}{17+0} \\  & =-\frac{x+3}{17}.\end{aligned}
$$

This is not a constant, which means that $y=f(x)$ does not have a horizontal asymptote.
